title: Christmas Cookie Bars
blurb: A sugar cookie base gone soft and thick, then frosted like a bar instead of iced like a cookie — the dough is meant to look underbaked when it comes out.

ingredients.note: softened to room temperature, for the bars
Christmas jimmies, plus more for garnish
softened to room temperature, for the frosting
room temperature, plus more as needed

steps: Preheat oven to 325°F. Spray a 9×13-inch pan with nonstick spray and line with parchment paper, letting it hang over the sides.
In a stand mixer, beat the butter, cream cheese and granulated sugar together on medium speed until light and creamy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Mix in the egg, egg yolk, vanilla and almond extract until smooth and well combined, scraping down the bowl as needed.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt and baking soda. Gradually add to the wet ingredients on low speed until a soft dough forms — it will be noticeably softer than a normal cookie dough, and that's correct. Fold in the sprinkles.

Press the dough evenly into the prepared pan with an offset spatula. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the center looks just set — don't overbake, or the bars won't stay soft and chewy as they cool.
Let the bars cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before frosting.

For the frosting, beat the butter until smooth. Add the vanilla, almond extract and salt, then gradually mix in the powdered sugar. Add the heavy cream and beat 1 to 2 minutes until light and fluffy. Tint with food coloring, if desired.
Spread the frosting over the cooled bars and top with additional sprinkles. Slice into squares to serve.
